intro: は and も sit in the same place in a sentence and both swallow が and を, so they compete for the same slot. The question is how the new item relates to what came before. も says "this one is the same": it adds an item to a statement already made. は says "as for this one": it picks out a topic and, when there is a comparison, sets it against the others.

skills.rule: If the same statement already holds for something else, use も ("too, either"); if you are introducing a topic or saying something different about it, use は.
skills.explain:
Ask these questions in order.

1. Has the same thing been said, or is it understood, about something else? If the new item shares it exactly, use も: 兄は医者です。弟も医者です. This works for negatives too, where English says "either": 肉は食べません。魚も食べません.

2. Does the new item get a different or opposite comment? Use は, which contrasts it with the first: 兄は医者です。弟は先生です. 肉は食べませんが、魚は食べます.

3. Nothing to compare with? Use は for the topic.

The position rules are the same for both: は and も replace が and を, and go after other particles (東京には, 東京にも), never before them. They never stack: no はも. In replies, "me too" and "me neither" are both 私もです; 私は is wrong there, because it says you are the odd one out.
patterns: A は X。B も X。  "B too / B either"
A は X。B は Y。  "but B is different"
[noun] に / で / と + は / も

examples.jp: 兄[あに]は医者[いしゃ]です。弟[おとうと]{も}医者[いしゃ]です。
examples.en: My older brother is a doctor. My younger brother is a doctor too.

examples.jp: 兄[あに]は医者[いしゃ]です。弟[おとうと]{は}先生[せんせい]です。
examples.en: My older brother is a doctor. My younger brother is a teacher.

examples.jp: 肉[にく]は食[た]べません。魚[さかな]{も}食[た]べません。
examples.en: I don't eat meat. I don't eat fish either.

examples.jp: 肉[にく]は食[た]べませんが、魚[さかな]{は}食[た]べます。
examples.en: I don't eat meat, but fish I do eat.

examples.jp: 平日[へいじつ]は忙[いそが]しいですが、週末[しゅうまつ]{は}暇[ひま]です。
examples.en: I'm busy on weekdays, but I'm free at the weekend.

examples.jp: 旅行[りょこう]で京都[きょうと]に行[い]きました。奈良[なら]に{も}行[い]きました。
examples.en: On the trip I went to Kyoto. I went to Nara as well.

contrast.note: Same comment, new item: "too" in positives, "either" in negatives. The predicate must match what was said before.
New topic or contrast: the comment differs from, or is set against, what was said about something else.

mistakes.bad: 姉[あね]は背[せ]が高[たか]いです。妹[いもうと]{も}背[せ]が低[ひく]いです。
mistakes.good: 姉[あね]は背[せ]が高[たか]いです。妹[いもうと]{は}背[せ]が低[ひく]いです。
mistakes.note: The sister is short, the opposite of tall: that is a contrast, so は.

mistakes.bad: 「田中[たなか]さんは行[い]きません。」「私[わたし]{は}行[い]きません。」
mistakes.good: 「田中[たなか]さんは行[い]きません。」「私[わたし]{も}行[い]きません。」
mistakes.note: "I'm not going either" repeats the same statement: も. With は it sounds as if you are the exception.

mistakes.bad: 東京[とうきょう]{も}に行[い]きました。
mistakes.good: 東京[とうきょう]に{も}行[い]きました。
mistakes.note: も and は come after に, で, と and から, never before them.

skills.tip: Same comment as before? も. Different comment, or nothing before? は.
